old: have something for you as a keepsake from Helen’s hand
new: have something for you as a keepsake from my own hand
reason: Helen is the speaker ("I too, my son," she said), but mid-sentence she refers to herself in the third person as "Helen’s hand." On audio, a first-time listener may briefly think a second woman is being introduced rather than recognizing self-reference.

old: They swayed the yoke on their necks and traveled all day long
new: The horses strained against the yoke on their necks and traveled all day long
reason: "Swayed the yoke" is an unclear, ambiguous verb choice for a modern reader/listener — it's not obvious whether the horses are shaking it off, straining against it, or something else. The image of horses running hard doesn't land clearly.

old: He quarreled with his father and went to live in Hyperesia
new: Polypheides quarreled with his father and went to live in Hyperesia
reason: The pronoun "He" is ambiguous: the immediately preceding clause names both Apollo and Amphiaraus (who has just died), and "his father" adds a second unnamed referent. A first-time listener has no way to resolve that "He" means Polypheides without replaying the sentence.

old: Eos, enthroned in gold, carried off Cleitus for his beauty’s sake
new: Dawn, enthroned in gold, carried off Cleitus for his beauty’s sake
reason: The dawn goddess is introduced earlier in this same Book as "Dawn, the rosy-fingered child of morning" (paragraph 15) but here is suddenly called "Eos" with no link back to that identity. A listener has no way to know this is the same figure, and "Eos" alone reads as an unexplained proper name.

old: hoisted their white sails with sheets of twisted oxhide
new: hoisted their white sails with ropes of twisted oxhide
reason: "Sheets" is nautical jargon for ropes/lines, but a general reader will default to the everyday meaning (cloth/paper) and picture something like fabric strips holding up the sail, which is confusing and inaccurate to the intended image.
